purpose: Bounded finite measured tests requested by M6 Pass C for Lynde: 1/2/3 self-Curse upkeep stacks with best ordering (Thirst, Bloodletting, Misfortunes, Cruel Reality, Torment of Scarabs, Death's Hold), Braids/Scepter/exile/DFC/copy timing cases, extra-upkeep supply with and without the selected copy engines, removal-and-return of the cuts versus the adds, and the seeded deployment cost of the selected swaps and staged alternatives. Seeded goldfish deployment model and exhaustive rules-encoded scenario grids; not a game simulation, not a source-bound game-engine receipt and not a win rate.

B1_self_curse_upkeep_stack_best_ordering.notes: Frozen-cache Oracle with the listed Curses attached to you (Lynde returns every Curse put into your graveyard attached to you at the next end step). All your upkeep triggers are ordered by you (CR 503.1a, 603.3b); the grid enumerates every order, every Lynde move target and the optional Misfortunes fetch (modelled as a harmless Curse attached to you) and keeps the best line (keep Lynde, keep the other creature, least life lost, most cards). Cruel Reality's trigger fixes 'that player' when it triggers, so moving it with Lynde does not stop that upkeep's sacrifice. Curse of Thirst counts Curses attached to you on resolution and Bloodletting doubles it if still attached. Torment of Scarabs is paid by sacrificing a Curse attached to you (Lynde returns it). Curse of Death's Hold applies -1/-1 when it returns at the end step, so an X/1 (Nightscape Familiar 1/1) dies before the upkeep. Unweighted cells, not frequencies.

cases.case: Despotic Scepter or Claws of Gix destroys/sacrifices your Curse in your main phase
cases.result: Lynde returns it at the beginning of your end step attached to you; it can be moved at your next upkeep (one-turn latency).

cases.case: Braids, Arisen Nightmare sacrifices a Curse at the beginning of your end step
cases.result: Lynde's delayed trigger is created after 'the beginning of the end step' has passed, so the Curse returns at the NEXT end step (the next opponent's turn), still attached to you before your next upkeep: same one-turn latency; opponents each sacrifice an enchantment or lose 2 while you draw.

cases.case: An opponent destroys a Curse attached to them during their turn
cases.result: It returns attached to you at that turn's end step; at your upkeep Lynde moves it again for two cards.

cases.case: The Curse card is exiled from your graveyard before the end step (Bojuka Bog, Relic)
cases.result: The delayed trigger finds nothing; the Curse is lost.

cases.case: Accursed Witch // Infectious Curse: Infectious Curse is put into your graveyard
cases.result: Lynde triggers (it was a Curse on the battlefield, 603.10a). In the graveyard the card has only its front-face characteristics (712.8a), a creature, not an Aura; an effect that puts a non-Aura onto the battlefield attached to a player puts it onto the battlefield unattached (303.4h), so Accursed Witch returns as a creature and its dies trigger can make Infectious Curse again.

cases.case: Copy Enchantment or Mirrormade copying a Curse is put into your graveyard
cases.result: Lynde triggers (look-back). The card returns; as it enters it may copy an enchantment on the battlefield; if it copies a Curse it enters as an Aura attached to you (the attachment Lynde specifies is legal for enchant player); if it copies a non-Aura it enters unattached (303.4h). Classified rules-encoded, moderate confidence.

cases.case: Court of Vantress (monarch) or Extravagant Replication makes a token copy of a Curse
cases.result: The token Aura is not cast, so you choose the player it enchants as it enters (303.4f): attach it to yourself and Lynde moves it to an opponent at the same or next upkeep for two cards, or attach it straight to an opponent.

cases.case: A token copy of a Curse is put into your graveyard
cases.result: Lynde triggers, but the token ceases to exist (704.5d, 111.7) and nothing returns.

cases.case: Court of Vantress while you are not the monarch becomes a copy of a Curse
cases.result: It is an Aura attached to nothing and goes to the graveyard (704.5m); Lynde returns the Court of Vantress card at the next end step unattached (303.4h) and its enters trigger makes you the monarch again. Rules-encoded, moderate confidence; not relied on for the selection.

The token Haze enters attached to the player you choose (303.4f): on yourself it gives one more additional upkeep from the next turn; Haze copies stack (each is 'enchanted player's first upkeep each turn').

cases.case: Extravagant Replication or Court copying a legendary permanent (Lynde, Obeka, The Ninth Doctor, Braids)
cases.result: Legend rule (704.5j): one is put into the graveyard. Not a useful target.

cases.case: Cruel Reality attached to you at your upkeep
cases.result: Its trigger makes YOU sacrifice a creature or planeswalker (Lynde if she is your only one) even if Lynde moves it first, because 'that player' is fixed when it triggers.

B3_extra_upkeep_and_copy_engine_supply.notes: One of your turns. Upkeeps = 1 + Paradox Haze + The Ninth Doctor (only if it becomes untapped during your untap step) + Obeka's combat damage (2 power, after combat). At each upkeep the copy-engine trigger is ordered before Lynde's, its Curse token is attached to you (303.4f) and Lynde moves one Curse attached to you for two cards. Not-monarch Court is counted as producing no token (its become-a-copy mode is not modelled). Unweighted cells; the copy target is assumed to exist (any Curse you control for Replication, any enchantment for Court).

B4_removal_and_return_cut_versus_add.notes: With Lynde on the battlefield a destroyed or sacrificed Curse returns attached to YOU. Cruel Reality then costs you a creature at your next upkeep (Lynde if alone); Curse of Death's Hold shrinks your creatures (Nightscape Familiar dies, Lynde 1/3) until Lynde moves it. Court of Vantress and Extravagant Replication are not Curses and never return to you. Unweighted cells.
